step_name: Audit 02 Guide Expected Behavior To Runtime Surfaces
step_goal: Audit whether the proposed HSConfig architecture actually turns guide-expected behavior into supported runtime config surfaces without silent omission, and identify where the current lowering path is still conservative.
produced_outputs: A machine-readable verdict that the proposed architecture is directionally correct but not yet fully non-conservative in the current lowering implementation.
A required surface-routing checklist: every guide claim must end up in Mulligan.json, CARDID.json, Combo.json, GlobalValues.json, or an explicit report-only artifact.

A blocker list for the still-conservative paths: narrow Mulligan condition safety, narrow CARDID emission, same-turn-only combo authoring, report-only GlobalValues intent, and blocked Presume or Concede runtime surfaces.
reliable_uses: Prove that the proposed architecture is explicitly non-silent at the contract layer: Step 05 requires gameplan, card obligation, coverage, and contract-gap artifacts before runtime file emission.

Prove that every deck card is expected to be checked against gameplan semantics before emission, because the deck-research and gameplan schemas require either explicit per-card semantics or an explicit visible gap for each deck card.

Prove that guide-backed opening-hand expectations can reach Mulligan.json in the current design, because unconditional keeps and throws emit directly and conditional keeps emit when the condition survives the runtime-safe Mulligan gate.
Prove that concrete ordered sequences can reach Combo.json when at least two exact CardIDs exist and the sequence is concrete enough to lower into documented runtime syntax.

Prove that unsupported or runtime-unsafe claims are designed to stay visible rather than disappear silently, because the current repo emits suppression reports for Mulligan and Combo claims and blocks unsupported runtime surfaces with explicit errors.
Prove that the runtime syntax model recognizes the full documented CARDID.json block family, including target, choice, hero power, attack, upgrade, and priority surfaces.

Prove that the current implementation is still conservative on CARDID lowering, because preview authoring only materializes BeforePlayCardBonus rows from a narrow card_usage subset instead of lowering the broader documented block family.
Prove that the design already separates semantic richness from runtime authority, which is the correct prerequisite for a future fully non-conservative compiler.
limitations: This audit can confirm the intended architecture and the live conservative boundaries, but it cannot claim that a not-yet-written HSConfig compiler already emits every documented runtime surface.

The current Mulligan.json path is conservative: runtime-safe conditions are limited to a small whitelist in mulligan_runtime_safety.py, so broader guide conditions remain suppressed even when official docs describe richer generic JSON conditions.

The current CARDID.json path is conservative: syntax validation allows the full documented block family, but preview authoring currently emits only BeforePlayCardBonus rows and does not yet lower documented target, discover, choose-one, Adapt, hero-power, attack, end-turn, upgrade, or priority behavior from gameplan semantics into runtime files.

The current Combo.json path is partly conservative: it requires at least two concrete CardIDs and currently joins emitted sequences with same-turn >>, so explicit cross-turn >-> authoring is an architecture requirement rather than a completed implementation.
The current GlobalValues.json path is conservative by policy: it materializes the runtime baseline and keeps research-only GlobalValues intent report-only until fresh runtime evidence exists.

Documented but registry-known unsupported Concede.json and Presume.json surfaces are visible and intentionally fail closed, so the design is non-silent there but not fully runtime-surface-complete in the current package.
aggressive_generation_policy: Every decoded deck card must resolve to one of two visible states before handoff: emitted runtime rows on a documented surface, or an explicit report-only gap or suppression row. Silent omission is forbidden.

Expected mulligan guidance should compile into Mulligan.json whenever the guide claim can be expressed with documented syntax; the compiler should broaden beyond the current tiny whitelist by using a capability matrix tied to officially documented patterns rather than a handful of hard-coded regex cases.

Expected target, use, hold, choice, hero-power, and attack behavior should compile into the most specific documented CARDID.json block instead of being flattened into generic BeforePlayCardBonus rows or dropped.

Concrete same-turn and cross-turn sequences should compile into Combo.json with an explicit operator field; symbolic synergy notes should stay visible in suppression artifacts instead of being guessed into runtime rows.

GlobalValues should remain baseline-first, but guide-backed overlay candidates should still appear in a report-only contract when runtime authority is intentionally withheld, so the architecture stays visible instead of silently conservative.

Unsupported surfaces such as Presume.json and Concede.json should remain fail-closed for runtime emission today, but their intent must still be surfaced in report-only artifacts with explicit reasons.
validation_gates: Every deck card must be represented either by emitted semantics or by an explicit contract gap, with no unaccounted card IDs.
Every guide-backed mulligan claim must end up in either Mulligan.json or mulligan_condition_suppression_report.json.
Every guide-backed per-card behavior claim that maps to documented syntax must end up in a CARDID.json row or in card_behavior_suppression_report.json with an explicit reason.
Every concrete combo claim with two or more exact CardIDs must end up in Combo.json or combo_suppression_report.json with an explicit reason.
Every emitted row must have exactly one provenance mapping back to a gameplan clause and a documented source-doc key.
Generated runtime files must pass strict JSON validation, GameCardId and filename validation, and supported-surface validation in visionai_model.py.
Aggregate CardBehavior.json may exist only as a preview report and must never be treated as a runtime package file.
Registry-known unsupported surfaces Presume.json and Concede.json must fail the runtime-support gate explicitly rather than being silently ignored.
architectural_implications: The proposed architecture passes the contract-design test: it already requires a semantic control plane, per-card coverage, provenance, and visible suppressions before runtime emission.
The proposed architecture does not yet pass the full runtime-surface test in the live implementation, because the current authoring path is still narrower than the documented VisionAI surface model.

A fully non-conservative HSConfig implementation needs a dedicated card-behavior surface router that lowers gameplan semantics into the full documented CARDID.json block family instead of only BeforePlayCardBonus.

A fully non-conservative HSConfig implementation needs an option-identity resolver for Discover, Choose One, Adapt, hero-power variants, and upgrade ownership before those documented blocks can be emitted safely.
A fully non-conservative HSConfig implementation needs a richer Mulligan capability matrix than the current regex whitelist, while still keeping load-safe validation as a hard gate.
A fully non-conservative HSConfig implementation needs an explicit combo operator model so same-turn and cross-turn sequences stay concrete instead of collapsing into same-turn-only authoring.

The current repo already provides the right hard boundaries for supported runtime surfaces, strict JSON validation, and explicit unsupported-surface errors, so HSConfig should extend lowering breadth without relaxing those safety gates.

The correct bottom line for this audit is partial pass: the architecture is non-silent and structurally aligned with the requirement, but the live lowering layer is still conservative in exactly the places the audit was meant to detect.
recommended_contracts: config_surface_intent_map.json to route every accepted guide claim into Mulligan.json, CARDID.json, Combo.json, GlobalValues.json, or report-only suppression.
card_gameplan_coverage_report.json to prove that every deck card was checked against gameplan semantics before runtime lowering.
card_obligation_matrix.json to preserve per-card use, hold, target, and anti-pattern expectations even when a runtime row is not emitted yet.
card_behavior_intent_map.json to map each per-card claim to owner card id, documented CARDID.json block, condition expression, value expression, and source provenance.
card_behavior_suppression_report.json to record every documented-but-not-yet-lowered CARDID claim instead of silently omitting it.
mulligan_compiler_capabilities.json to encode which documented Mulligan selectors and condition families are safe to emit for the current runtime package.
combo_surface_contract.json with exact card sequences, same_turn or cross_turn operator, source refs, and emission status.
runtime_surface_support_matrix.json to keep supported runtime surfaces separate from registry-known unsupported surfaces.
report_only_guidance_registry.json to preserve strategic claims that are source-backed but not safely emittable today.
never_autogenerate_without: Exact deck identity, resolved CardIDs, and a validated gameplan contract with explicit per-card semantics or explicit visible gaps.
A supported-surface registry that distinguishes card behavior, mulligan, combo, and global values from registry-known unsupported Presume or Concede surfaces.
A documented lowering path for every emitted CARDID.json block, including file ownership for option cards, hero powers, and branch cards when needed.
A runtime-safe Mulligan condition decision for every conditional keep or throw, with suppression reporting when the claim is source-backed but not yet safe to emit.
At least two exact CardIDs and an explicit order for every emitted Combo.json row.
Strict JSON and preview validation over every emitted runtime document, including GameCardId and provenance checks.
A mandatory suppression or gap-reporting path for every guide claim that cannot be emitted safely today.
